claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2026-02 reports: In southeastern Oruro and northern Potosí, models project drier dry seasons and wetter wet seasons with more floods and droughts; Quechua and Aymara highland farmers rely on rainfed or small-irrigation systems.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2026-02 reports: The report attributes the 2023 highland drought to climate-related heat and El Niño: water flows fell one-third, and crop losses affected nearly two million farmers across seven departments including Oruro and Potosí.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: Attribution to heat and El Niño is the case study's account, not an independently inspected event-attribution analysis. The farmer count covers seven departments, not only the project area.

claim_decisions.statement: REDESCA's 2025 report says 2024 fires threatened Ayoreo people in voluntary isolation in the Chaco. It warns habitat destruction could force unwanted outside contact, exposing people to disease and violence; the extent of damage to uncontacted Ayoreo territory was unknown.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: Conditional rights/protection risk, not an observed contact or violence event. Fire ignition is not attributed to climate change. Protection must respect the choice to remain uncontacted.

pathways.climate_pressure: 2024 wildfire hazard in the Chaco; ignition is not attributed here to climate change.
pathways.documented_impact: Fire threatens habitat used by Ayoreo people in voluntary isolation.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Habitat destruction could force unwanted contact where territorial and non-contact safeguards are inadequate.
pathways.possible_consequence: Conditional exposure to violence and disease and threats to physical/cultural survival; no contact or violence event is asserted.
alternative_explanations: Land-use pressures and deforestation also affect habitat independently of climate.
Extent of damage in uncontacted territory was unknown to the mission.
pathways.uncertainty: Source-stated conditional protection mechanism, not a verified violence outcome, precise exposure map or anthropogenic attribution of the fires.
resilience_factors: Territorial protection and fire prevention must respect peoples' right to remain in voluntary isolation; do not use this pathway to justify forced contact.
pathways.compact_statement: Wildfire habitat loss could force unwanted contact and heighten violence risk for isolated Ayoreo; REDESCA does not report that this occurred.

gaps: The Ayoreo pathway is a conditional protection risk grounded in REDESCA, not a report of unwanted contact or observed violence; prevention must respect non-contact.
A generic drought-crisis/social-conflict illustration is not treated as a demonstrated urban conflict pathway.

executive_assessment.text: Highland examples distinguish Oruro/Potosí Indigenous farming, ayllu governance and irrigation maintenance; urban water evidence concerns historical La Paz/El Alto droughts.
Wildfire evidence identifies named lowland Indigenous territories and San Ignacio de Velasco water constraints. Ayoreo protection risks are conditional and require non-contact safeguards.

Camiri/Kaami planning and WFP Oruro evaluation summaries provide capacities and limits; participation, spending allocations and short-term consumption protection do not establish lasting resilience or peace effects.
